```{r}
parsed

GasArticles

# building function
Query_News <- function(search, from_date, api_key) {
  response <- GET(
    url = "https://newsapi.org/v2/everything",
    query = list(
      q = search,
      from = from_date,
      language = "en",
      pageSize = 30,
      apikey = api_key
    )
  )
}

#testing function

testresponse1 <- Query_News("Midterm", "2026-08-30", my_api_key)
str(testresponse1, max.level = 1)


testresponse2 <- Query_News("Energy", "2026-08-30", my_api_key)
str(testresponse2, max.level = 1)
```

### Task 2

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Reading in dataset
url <- "https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/online/datasets/635USrollercoasters.csv"
coasters <- read_csv(url)


RollerCoasters <- coasters %>%
  mutate(
    State = as.factor(State),
    'Census Region' = as.factor('Census Region'),
    AgeGroup = factor(AgeGroup, levels = c(1, 2, 3), labels = c("Older", "Recent", "Newest")),
    Scale = as.factor(Scale),
    Type = as.factor(Type),
    Design = as.factor(Design),
    Inversions = as.factor("Inversions?"),
    Make = as.factor(Make)
  )

#RollerCoasters




```

```{r}
glimpse(coasters) # viewing data contents

missing_report <- coasters %>%
  summarize(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Missing_Count") %>%
  filter(Missing_Count > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(Missing_Count))

missing_report #missing values 

# Contingency Tables

#tne-way table: Type
table_1way <- table(Type = coasters$Type)
table_1way

# two-way table: Type vs Scale
table_2way <- table(Type = coasters$Type, Scale = coasters$Scale)
table_2way

# three-way table: Type vs Scale vs AgeGroup
table_3way <- table(
  Type = coasters$Type,
  Scale = coasters$Scale,
  AgeGroup = coasters$AgeGroup
)
table_3way

```
Interpretation: From the one way table - this means there are 530 steel roller coasters.

From the two-way table - There are 216 extreme steel coasters.

From the three-way table - There are 8 Older, Extreme, steel coasters.


```{r}
# Method 1:
coasters %>%
  filter(Type == "Steel") %>%
  with(table(Scale, AgeGroup))

# Method 2:
table_3way <- table(
  Type = coasters$Type,
  Scale = coasters$Scale,
  AgeGroup = coasters$AgeGroup
)
table_3way["Steel", , ]
```
```{r}
# Two-way with dplyr
coasters %>%
  filter(!is.na(Type), !is.na(Scale)) %>%
  group_by(Type, Scale) %>%
  summarize(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Scale, values_from = Count, values_fill = 0)


# 1. Stacked Bar Graph
ggplot(data = filter(coasters, !is.na(Type), !is.na(Scale)), aes(x = Scale, fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(position = "stack") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Coaster Scales by Construction Type (Stacked)",
    x = "Scale Category",
    y = "Number of Coasters",
    fill = "Coaster Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# 2. Side-by-Side (Clustered) Bar Graph
ggplot(data = filter(coasters, !is.na(Type), !is.na(Scale)), aes(x = Scale, fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Coaster Types Across Scales (Side-by-Side)",
    x = "Scale Category",
    y = "Number of Coasters",
    fill = "Coaster Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


```
